authors: Chen, Mark; Tworek, Jerry; Jun, Heewoo; Yuan, Qiming; et al.
title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
notes: arXiv:2107.03374 (58 authors). arXiv-only; no peer-reviewed venue.
about: Introduces Codex, a GPT model fine-tuned on public GitHub code, and the HumanEval benchmark of functional correctness. Codex solves 28.8% of HumanEval problems with a single sample and 70.2% with 100 samples per problem.

authors: Austin, Jacob; Odena, Augustus; Nye, Maxwell; Bosma, Maarten; Michalewski, Henryk; Dohan, David; Jiang, Ellen; Cai, Carrie; Terry, Michael; Le, Quoc; Sutton, Charles
title: Program Synthesis with Large Language Models
notes: arXiv:2108.07732. arXiv-only.
about: Evaluates language models of 244M to 137B parameters on two new benchmarks, MBPP and MathQA-Python, in few-shot and fine-tuning regimes. Synthesis performance scales log-linearly with model size.

authors: Li, Yujia; Choi, David; Chung, Junyoung; Kushman, Nate; et al.
title: Competition-level code generation with AlphaCode
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science
notes: 26 authors per Crossref.
about: AlphaCode generates very large numbers of candidate programs with transformer models, then filters and clusters them down to at most 10 submissions. It achieved an average ranking in the top 54.3% in simulated Codeforces competitions.

authors: Peng, Sida; Kalliamvakou, Eirini; Cihon, Peter; Demirer, Mert
title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
notes: arXiv:2302.06590. arXiv version used; no journal version confirmed.
about: Controlled experiment in which recruited developers implemented an HTTP server in JavaScript. The treatment group with access to GitHub Copilot completed the task 55.8% faster than the control group.

authors: Ziegler, Albert; Kalliamvakou, Eirini; Li, X. Alice; Rice, Andrew; Rifkin, Devon; Simister, Shawn; Sittampalam, Ganesh; Aftandilian, Edward
title: Productivity assessment of neural code completion
container: Proceedings of the 6th ACM SIGPLAN International Symposium on Machine Programming (MAPS '22)
about: Case study that asked GitHub Copilot users about its impact on their productivity and compared their perceptions with usage data. The acceptance rate of shown suggestions, rather than the persistence of completions in the code, drives perceived productivity.

authors: Ziegler, Albert; Kalliamvakou, Eirini; Li, X. Alice; Rice, Andrew; Rifkin, Devon; Simister, Shawn; Sittampalam, Ganesh; Aftandilian, Edward
title: Measuring GitHub Copilot's Impact on Productivity
notes: Journal version of the MAPS 2022 case study by the same authors.
about: Case study that asks Copilot users about its impact on their productivity and looks for their perceptions in user data.

authors: Barke, Shraddha; James, Michael B.; Polikarpova, Nadia
title: Grounded Copilot: How Programmers Interact with Code-Generating Models
container: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages
notes: Pages as given by Crossref. UNCONFIRMED: article number (PACMPL uses article numbers; believed to be Article 78).
about: Grounded theory analysis of 20 participants solving programming tasks in four languages with Copilot. Interactions are bimodal: in acceleration mode the programmer knows what to do and uses Copilot to get there faster; in exploration mode they use it to explore options.

authors: Vaithilingam, Priyan; Zhang, Tianyi; Glassman, Elena L.
title: Expectation vs. Experience: Evaluating the Usability of Code Generation Tools Powered by Large Language Models
container: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems Extended Abstracts (CHI EA '22)
notes: 7 pages per Crossref. UNCONFIRMED: ACM article number.
about: Within-subjects user study with 24 participants using Copilot. Copilot did not necessarily improve task completion time or success rate, but most participants preferred it as a useful starting point; understanding, editing and debugging its code was difficult.

authors: Liang, Jenny T.; Yang, Chenyang; Myers, Brad A.
title: A Large-Scale Survey on the Usability of AI Programming Assistants: Successes and Challenges
container: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 46th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE '24)
notes: 13 pages per Crossref. UNCONFIRMED: ACM article number.
about: Survey of 410 developers analysed qualitatively and quantitatively. Developers mainly use assistants to reduce keystrokes, finish tasks quickly and recall syntax; they avoid them when the output misses functional or non-functional requirements or is hard to control.

authors: Mozannar, Hussein; Bansal, Gagan; Fourney, Adam; Horvitz, Eric
title: Reading Between the Lines: Modeling User Behavior and Costs in AI-Assisted Programming
container: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '24)
notes: 16 pages per Crossref. UNCONFIRMED: ACM article number.
about: Develops CUPS, a taxonomy of programmer activities when interacting with Copilot. A study of 21 programmers who retrospectively labelled their sessions revealed inefficiencies and time costs.

authors: Ross, Steven I.; Martinez, Fernando; Houde, Stephanie; Muller, Michael; Weisz, Justin D.
title: The Programmer's Assistant: Conversational Interaction with a Large Language Model for Software Development
container: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI '23)
about: Prototype conversational programming assistant evaluated with 42 participants. Despite sceptical initial expectations, participants were impressed by the breadth of its capabilities, the quality of its responses and its potential for productivity.

authors: Moradi Dakhel, Arghavan; Majdinasab, Vahid; Nikanjam, Amin; Khomh, Foutse; Desmarais, Michel C.; Jiang, Zhen Ming (Jack)
title: GitHub Copilot AI pair programmer: Asset or Liability?
notes: Article number 111734. Preprint arXiv:2206.15331 (abstract read there).
about: Evaluates Copilot on fundamental algorithmic problems and against human solutions to programming tasks. Human solutions had a higher correct ratio, but Copilot's buggy solutions needed less effort to repair.

authors: Pearce, Hammond; Ahmad, Baleegh; Tan, Benjamin; Dolan-Gavitt, Brendan; Karri, Ramesh
title: Asleep at the Keyboard? Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot's Code Contributions
container: 2022 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
about: Prompts Copilot with 89 scenarios based on high-risk CWE weaknesses, producing 1,689 programs. Approximately 40% of them were found to be vulnerable.

authors: Perry, Neil; Srivastava, Megha; Kumar, Deepak; Boneh, Dan
title: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?
container: Proceedings of the 2023 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS '23)
about: User study of security-related programming tasks. Participants with access to an AI assistant wrote significantly less secure code and were more likely to believe their code was secure.

authors: Sandoval, Gustavo; Pearce, Hammond; Nys, Teo; Karri, Ramesh; Garg, Siddharth; Dolan-Gavitt, Brendan
title: Lost at C: A User Study on the Security Implications of Large Language Model Code Assistants
notes: arXiv:2208.09727. No DOI. Pages from the USENIX BibTeX as reported in search results.
about: Security-driven user study (N=58) in which student programmers implemented a singly-linked list in C with or without LLM assistance. AI-assisted users produced critical security bugs at a rate no greater than 10% more than the control.

authors: Forsgren, Nicole; Storey, Margaret-Anne; Maddila, Chandra; Zimmermann, Thomas; Houck, Brian; Butler, Jenna
title: The SPACE of Developer Productivity
about: Argues that developer productivity cannot be measured by a single metric or dimension and presents the SPACE framework, showing how it can be used to understand productivity in practice and to create better measures.

authors: Forsgren, Nicole; Humble, Jez; Kim, Gene
title: Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps: Building and Scaling High Performing Technology Organizations
notes: ISBN 9781942788331 (paperback). Source of the software delivery performance measures commonly called the DORA metrics.
about: Draws on four years of survey research, including State of DevOps data, to examine how software delivery performance is measured and what drives it.

authors: Bacchelli, Alberto; Bird, Christian
title: Expectations, outcomes, and challenges of modern code review
about: Observations, interviews, surveys and classification of review comments across teams at Microsoft. Finding defects is the main motivation, but reviews are less about defects than expected and bring knowledge transfer, team awareness and alternative solutions; understanding the change is the key challenge.

authors: Sadowski, Caitlin; Söderberg, Emma; Church, Luke; Sipko, Michal; Bacchelli, Alberto
title: Modern code review: a case study at Google
container: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Software Engineering: Software Engineering in Practice (ICSE-SEIP '18)
notes: Crossref title field gives only 'Modern code review'; UNCONFIRMED: subtitle wording taken from the usual citation, not re-checked on the ACM page.
about: Exploratory study of code review at Google using 12 interviews, a survey of 44 respondents and review logs for 9 million reviewed changes, covering motivations, current practices, satisfaction and challenges.

authors: Cunningham, Ward
title: The WyCash portfolio management system
container: Addendum to the Proceedings on Object-Oriented Programming Systems, Languages, and Applications (OOPSLA '92)
notes: Experience report usually cited as the origin of the technical debt metaphor.

authors: Kruchten, Philippe; Nord, Robert L.; Ozkaya, Ipek
title: Technical Debt: From Metaphor to Theory and Practice
notes: Introduction to an IEEE Software special issue on technical debt.

authors: Runeson, Per; Höst, Martin
title: Guidelines for conducting and reporting case study research in software engineering
notes: Published online December 2008; issue dated 2009.
about: Introduces case study methodology for software engineering, adapted from methodology handbooks in social science and information systems, and presents recommended practices and empirically derived checklists for researchers and readers.

authors: Braun, Virginia; Clarke, Victoria
title: Using thematic analysis in psychology
about: Presents thematic analysis as a method for identifying, analysing and reporting patterns in qualitative data, with a six-phase guide to conducting it.

authors: Ralph, Paul; bin Ali, Nauman; Baltes, Sebastian; Bianculli, Domenico; et al.
title: Empirical Standards for Software Engineering Research
notes: arXiv:2010.03525 (43 authors). The ACM SIGSOFT Empirical Standards are living documents; UNCONFIRMED: current web URL of the standards not checked.
about: Describes empirical standards, natural-language models of a community's expectations for specific kinds of study such as questionnaire surveys, generated by the ACM SIGSOFT Paper and Peer Review Quality Initiative.

authors: Creswell, John W.; Plano Clark, Vicki L.
title: Designing and Conducting Mixed Methods Research
notes: ISBN 9781483344379. UNCONFIRMED: year; SAGE dates the 3rd edition August 2017, library records give 2018.

authors: Easterbrook, Steve; Singer, Janice; Storey, Margaret-Anne; Damian, Daniela
title: Selecting Empirical Methods for Software Engineering Research
container: Guide to Advanced Empirical Software Engineering
notes: Book chapter. UNCONFIRMED: editors (believed Shull, Singer and Sjøberg; not in the Crossref record).

authors: Wohlin, Claes; Runeson, Per; Höst, Martin; Ohlsson, Magnus C.; Regnell, Björn; Wesslén, Anders
title: Experimentation in Software Engineering
notes: ISBN 9783642290435. UNCONFIRMED: edition statement (not in the Crossref record). Checked at: https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-29044-2

authors: Kocetkov, Denis; Li, Raymond; Ben Allal, Loubna; Li, Jia; et al.
title: The Stack: 3 TB of permissively licensed source code
notes: arXiv:2211.15533 (13 authors). arXiv version used. Relevant to licensing of code training data.
about: Introduces The Stack, a 3.1 TB dataset of permissively licensed source code in 30 programming languages, with a data governance plan. Training only on permissively licensed data can match previously reported HumanEval and MBPP performance.

authors: Li, Raymond; Ben Allal, Loubna; Zi, Yangtian; Muennighoff, Niklas; et al.
title: StarCoder: may the source be with you!
notes: arXiv:2305.06161 (67 authors). UNCONFIRMED: later journal publication (believed TMLR); cited here as arXiv.
about: The BigCode community introduces StarCoder and StarCoderBase, 15.5B-parameter code models trained on The Stack, a collection of permissively licensed GitHub repositories with inspection tools and an opt-out process.

authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
notes: Crossref lists Tabassi, Elham as author; usually cited with NIST as corporate author. Issued January 2023.
